subject: Data placement Qs + proposed action items (US / EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Data placement Qs + proposed action items (US / EU / APAC)

Hi Liam — great to meet today. Quick recap and the items we committed to follow up on after the call. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Call summary (very high-level):
- BrightPath wants to run inference for patient-facing triage in the US and EU; APAC is lower priority for phase 1.
- Primary concerns: PII handling (transient vs persisted), retention windows, and whether logs/trace data leave regional boundaries during failover.
- Desired behavior: prefer pinning to region for residency, automatic cross-region failover for availability, with clear controls for backups and audit logs.

Action items / questions we promised to clarify:
1) Residency enforcement: support for regional pinning by account or by route — we recommended account-level pinning for your use case (keeps traffic and storage in-region unless an explicit DR event triggers failover).
2) Cross-region failover behavior: in a failover, models can run in a warm standby region; we will confirm whether ephemeral logs are mirrored and what retention applies (preview: request-level logs can be configured not to replicate).
3) Backups & snapshots: confirm frequency and where immutable snapshots are stored; options for encrypted snapshots inside EU key materials.
4) PII and tokenization: outline approaches for prefix stripping, on-the-fly redaction, or customer-side pseudonymization.
5) Audit evidence: provide examples of logs/audit trails we can surface for SOC 2/contract review.

What I'll attach: a short one-pager on residency controls and a diagram for failover/backups.

Next steps:
- I will share the attachments (two files) and a short matrix that maps your ask to our config knobs.
- Ben will follow up with the technical profile we saw today (sequence lengths, concurrent requests) to recommend model variants and pin sizing.
- Please send any specific regulatory clauses you need (e.g., EU data export clause) so we can confirm contractual language.

Thanks again — available for a quick 20-min sync tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: redwood-data-residency-summary.pdf (1 page), maps_fallback_diagram.png (PNG)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightpath.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data placement Qs + proposed action items (US / EU / APAC)

Thanks, Jasmine — that matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from the engineering and security side: 

1) For EU production traffic, are there options to ensure logs containing metadata (request id, model version, latencies) are kept in-region and never replicated unless we opt in? We can tolerate non-PII metrics being aggregated globally, but any identifier that could be traced back to a user must remain in the EU.

2) During cross-region failover, does Redwood stream raw request payloads to the standby region before the failover event (i.e., continuous replication), or only route live traffic after failover? If there's any replication, we need to ensure we can disable it for EU traffic.

3) For backups: we require encrypted snapshots using our EU KMS keys — is there a way to supply our own key or integrate with our KMS?

Also, curious on estimated RTO for a region failover — what should we design for at the application layer?

If you can answer those 3 in-line, we'll review and then ask legal for a sample clause.

— Liam
CTO, BrightPath.ai
liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data placement Qs + proposed action items (US / EU / APAC)

Quick technical notes / proposed answers we can send back: 

- Logs replication: We can run request-level logging with a per-account flag that controls replication. By default, diagnostic/log metadata are local; we only mirror aggregated metrics for platform health. For EU-anchored accounts we can enable a strict "no-replication" policy for any fields marked as sensitive.

- Failover replication model: We do not continuously stream raw request payloads to standby regions for EU accounts unless the customer enables cross-region replication. Failover routing only sends live traffic to the standby when the primary region is unavailable. We will add a "pre-warm" option (replicate model weights only) if BrightPath needs lower RTO; this still keeps request logs local.

- KMS integration: We support customer-managed keys for snapshot encryption in dedicated/private deployments (Redwood Private). In hosted mode we offer envelope encryption and can support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for enterprise contracts — need to check specific EU KMS providers (Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS).

- RTO estimate: for warm-standby configuration we recommend designing for ~2-10 minutes to start serving, depending on model size and KV cache warmup. If they want <60s, suggest a full pre-warm with cached KV snapshot which increases cost.

I'll draft a short doc with config flags we can toggle (replication: on/off, snapshot storage: region, snapshot-KMS: BYOK/Redwood). Jasmine — want me to send that as the technical appendix?

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, security@brightpath.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data placement Qs + proposed action items (US / EU / APAC)

Hi Liam — putting Ben's notes into an action-oriented response below so you have clear answers to pass to security/legal. I've also attached the one-pager and diagram.

Answers (short):
1) Logs replication: Yes — we can enforce a per-account "no replication" policy that prevents request-level logs or any identifier marked sensitive from leaving the EU. Aggregated metrics (non-identifiable) are available globally for billing/health only.

2) Cross-region replication vs failover: No continuous raw request replication for EU accounts unless you explicitly opt into replication. Failover only routes live traffic after an outage. Optional pre-warm (weights + KV snapshot) can be enabled if you want faster RTO.

3) KMS/BYOK for backups: Supported in Redwood Private and on dedicated contracts; for hosted we can negotiate BYOK via enterprise onboarding. We will confirm supported providers for EU in a follow-up from security/infra (target: EOD Fri).

4) RTO guidance: plan for 2-10 minutes for warm standby; sub-60s requires full pre-warm which is more costly.

Next steps (for BrightPath):
- Liam / Security: confirm the exact legal clause or data export language you want us to flag so we can validate contract language.
- Jira: Ben will create a short tech appendix describing the three configuration flags and a sample json snippet.
- I will share a meeting invite for a 20-min technical call next week to walk security through the config and BYOK options.

Thanks — attaching:
- redwood-data-residency-summary.pdf
- maps_fallback_diagram.png

Best,
Jasmine
